subject: Access controls for customer data - RBAC, support access, break-glass (FinTrust)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintrust.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Access controls for customer data (RBAC, support access, break-glass)

Hi Samir / Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time today - very helpful conversation. Below is a concise recap of the access controls / data handling items we discussed and the proposed next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key requirements you called out:
- PII classification: Redwood must support field-level classification and a mechanism to redact/tokenize before logs/backups leave your environment.
- Data residency: production data stored and processed in US regions only (no EU/APAC replication for this tenant).
- Retention: primary retention policy 7 years for transaction records; shorter retention for derived analytics (30/90/365 days) depending on dataset.
- Logging & audit: per-request audit logs for data access (who/what/why), immutable retention for audit window, exportable CSV for compliance reviews.
- RBAC & least privilege: role-based access (admin, engineer, analyst) with fine-grained permissions, scoped to projects/environments.
- Support access / break-glass: time-limited, request-and-approve workflow for Redwood support; all break-glass events must be fully logged and notified to FinTrust security.

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
1) I attached a short RBAC questionnaire (FinTrust-RBAC-Questions.xlsx) to capture role mappings and typical user counts. Please populate and send back - that will let us scope the role permission matrix.
2) We'll prepare a draft SOW with explicit controls and a break-glass process for review (sending by EOD Thu).
3) Schedule a technical call with your security / infra team to validate KMS/HSM integration and retention workflows - are you available next week (Tue/Wed preferred)?

Notes / clarifications from the call:
- You said any support access will require an approval from two FinTrust approvers (security + product).
- FinTrust wants support break-glass to be auditable via KMS logs and immutable event logs for at least 2 years.

Attachments: FinTrust-RBAC-Questions.xlsx (please fill), short RBAC example matrix.

If this looks right I'll send the SOW draft and a proposed technical agenda.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fintrust.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Access controls for customer data (RBAC, support access, break-glass)

Hi Marissa, thanks for the clear recap. Confirmations / clarifications below: 

- PII: Correct - we need field-level classification and the ability to redact PII before any logs/backups are moved off our tenant. Tokenization is preferred.
- Retention: 7 years for transaction records is our baseline (regulated). For analytics datasets we can discuss tiering but aim for default 90 days unless otherwise specified.
- Data residency: US-only (primary region us-west-2). No secondary replication outside US without explicit written approval.
- RBAC: Our initial role definitions are Admin (~3), Platform Engineer (~5), Data Analyst (~12). We'll fill these in the spreadsheet.
- Support access / break-glass: Two approvers required (Security Director + Product Ops). Access must be time-limited (max 4 hours) and every event must auto-generate an immutable audit record plus immediate Slack/email notification to our security channel.

I attached a quick note with a couple of policy excerpts and Laura (cc) will fill the RBAC sheet this afternoon. We're happy to do a technical sync next Wed 10-11am PT if that works for your team.

Samir
Head of IT Security, FinTrust
samir.patel@fintrust.com | +1 650-555-0199

Attachments: FinTrust-PCI-Notes.txt

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Access controls for customer data (RBAC, support access, break-glass)

Marissa / Rishi - thanks for the notes. Quick internal take before we follow up with FinTrust security:

- RBAC: We can model the three roles Samir listed. We should propose permission scoping by project + environment; engineers get tokenized data for dev only, no PII in dev unless explicitly requested.
- Break-glass / support access: Recommend a time-limited, auditable workflow backed by a signed approval in our internal ticketing system (Jira) + temporary credential issuance via vault and KMS-wrapped keys. All events logged (immutable) and retention set to 2 years for the break-glass audit logs (meets their ask).
- Data residency: We will propose a tenant-level region lock (us-west-2).

Action items for Redwood ops/security:
- I'll draft the technical section for the SOW covering KMS integration, credential issuance, and log retention.
- Rishi, please prepare a short note on how we do redaction/tokenization and include any limitations (e.g., streaming inference corner cases).

Marissa - if Samir confirms Wed 10-11am PT for the technical sync, I can join and Rishi will be on the deep-dive.

Vivek
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

- Data retention defaults and policy options (7 years for regulated transactions; analytics tiering)
- RBAC matrix with proposed permissions mapped to FinTrust roles (sheet attached)
- Break-glass workflow: two-approver process, time-limited access, vault-based temporary creds, immutable audit logs (2-year retention), Slack/email notifications to your security channel
